newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU agrees to send advisory mission to Albania.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees to send advisory mission to Albania.

text.p: The European Union on Sunday agreed to send military and police advisers to Albania to help restore order, German diplomatic sources said.
They said there was also a consensus to provide protection for this mission if necessary, but this would not be a military operation. "Any interventionist approach is off the table," one source said.

"External assistance is needed immediately for the restoration of security, in particular in and around Tirana," EU foreign ministers said in a brief statement released at a two-day informal meeting in the Netherlands.

"Among the member states there was readiness to send an advisory mission in the civilian as well as the police and military fields," the statement said, adding that the mission would require a United Nations mandate.

The EU itself was to despatch a high-level mission to Tirana on Monday including representatives from the Netherlands, Greece, Italy, the European Commission and the Organisation for security and Cooperation in Europe.
The EU also called on Albania to take steps towards its own reconstruction.
